reviewSummary: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX. The subject is unmoved at 5ec291a5... mode 0444. Both turn-1 Claude findings and the unlabeled Codex turn-1 SHOULD-FIX land completely and correctly: the frozen turn-1 subject carried exactly two 'under D-294 Decision 1' attributions and turn 2 carries none, and the owner-selection count is corrected from three to four with occupancy v2 $.proposedLaterWork[4] supplied. All four enumerated sites were verified verbatim against frozen bytes and no fifth qualifying site exists. HEAD, D-340 adoption, last-heading custody, live COORD, file 08 and its DR-126/DR-G22/DR-107/DR-118 cells, required-now 28, Condition 2 at 5 of 32, Condition 4 at 28 of 28, the split no-cell-edit branch, both leftoverDesign partitions, all four frozen digests and every cited heading and commit reproduce. The act stays COORD-only, records no artifact successor and no platform-tcb leftover-join.v10, remasures nothing, invents no selector value and no identifier, leaves Q5 named, and marks nothing SATISFIED or QUALIFIED. One repair remains: the Protocol block's two custody citations for the frozen turn-1 verdicts are broken mid-token inside their code spans, so neither path resolves as written - a defect the immediately preceding adopted entry, D-340, avoids by keeping the same-shaped paths whole on overlong lines.

shouldFix.class: custody citation corrupted by a mid-token line wrap inside a code span
shouldFix.defect: Two frozen turn-1 review-artifact paths are broken mid-token inside their backticks across a blockquote line break. Line 12 ends '(`artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-341.review-adversarial.claude2' and line 13 is '> .json`'; line 16 ends '(`artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-341.review-adversarial.codex.j' and line 17 is '> son`'. A code span containing a line break renders the break as a single space, so these render as 'artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-341.review-adversarial.claude2 .json' and 'artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-341.review-adversarial.codex.j son'. Neither resolves; each half was tested and no such file exists.
shouldFix.precedent: D-340, the immediately preceding adopted entry, cites the same-shaped review paths whole on single lines of 75 and 73 characters, deliberately overflowing the ~69-character wrap the rest of its Status block observes. Live COORD has 46 lines where a code span spans a line break, and every one breaks at a space inside a natural-language phrase (for example `## 6. Non-negotiable implementation laws` and `Blueprint-readiness: conditions 1-5 evaluated; docs/v2/implementation authorized`), so the rendered content stays correct. No adopted entry splits a path token. The bare `artifacts/` prefix is itself correct house form (635 uses); the wrap, not the prefix, is the defect.
shouldFix.whyItMatters: The Protocol block exists to record custody of the two frozen turn-1 verdicts, and the path is the address. An adopted COORD entry is permanent, and this one would carry two custody addresses that do not name any file. It also introduces a wrap form the corpus has never adopted, which a later entry could copy.
shouldFix.loadBearing: No. The 64-hex digest pinned immediately after each path is correct and unambiguous, the Subject section carries every other path whole, and no heading, obligation, status token, count, or owner cell is misread. This is why it is SHOULD-FIX and not MUST-FIX.
shouldFix.repair: Keep each path on one line, letting the line overflow the wrap column as D-340 does; or cite the two basenames. Change nothing else - not the digests, the counts, the return-shape recitals, the four-site enumeration, or any other byte.

observations: The four-site correction is not merely arithmetic - it is verified. Each enumerated path was resolved in the frozen JSON and its sentence read: v45 $.platformProfile.populationPacket and occupancy v2 $.filesystems.laterAct both read 'Choosing its owner is a separate decision.'; occupancy v2 $.proposedLaterWork[4] reads 'Choosing that packet's owner is a separate decision.'; v9 $.proposedLaterWork[2] reads 'This join does not populate those selectors and does not choose that packet's owner.' The draft's disjunctive predicate now matches exactly the set it enumerates.

The draft renders the v9 site as 'the speaker does not choose that packet's owner' rather than quoting v9's own 'This join does not ...'. That is the right call: quoting the artifact's first-person deictic into COORD prose would produce exactly the 'This join' defect this lineage rejects on, and the paraphrase preserves the meaning without importing the voice.

The naming-parent sentence drops the house form's 'not leftover-join.vN' negative limb, which at first reading looks like an omission. It is not. The limb exists in entries that record a leftover-join successor and must disclaim it as the naming parent; this entry records no successor and takes last-heading custody only, so naming 'not leftover-join.v9' would gratuitously import DR-126 join lineage into a COORD-only act. 'D-086 named the identifier.' is independently confirmed by file 08 line 358.

Codex's turn-1 repair asked the draft to state 'three' frozen sentences while Claude's asked for four. The draft resolves the tension correctly rather than splitting it: it adopts four, which is what the bytes support, and satisfies every substantive element of Codex's repair text. Codex's finding charged the authority attribution, not the count, so nothing of it is left unlanded.
